title: Indreshwor Mahadev
description: The origins of the sacred Indreshwar Mahadev Temple are deeply rooted in ancient Hindu mythology, reflecting themes of desire, repentance, and divine forgiveness. According to legend, Lord Indra, the king of the gods, was once cursed by the revered sage Rishi Gautama. The curse came as a consequence of Indra\’s misconduct, when he, captivated by Ahilya, took advantage of the sage\’s absence and deceived her.

Overcome with guilt and burdened by the curse, Lord Indra sought a path to redemption. He journeyed to the serene land of Panauti, a place known for its spiritual energy and natural beauty. There, he performed intense penance and deep meditation, dedicating himself to the worship of Lord Shiva, the supreme ascetic and destroyer of sins.

Moved by Indra\’s unwavering devotion and sincere repentance, Lord Shiva eventually granted him forgiveness and lifted the curse. The sacred spot where this profound act of penance took place came to be revered as the Indreshwar Mahadev Temple—its name derived from Indra himself. Over time, this temple has become not only a symbol of divine grace but also a reminder that even the mightiest can find redemption through humility and devotion.
